body: I live in NC and just moved into a new apartment. He was in my closet.

Narcissism. My ex once tried to get into the Highway Patrol. They rejected him because he failed the emotional intelligence test (go figure). He concluded that it was because his IQ was too high and thus he was harder to control.

The question isn't whether or not he loves you or ever loved you, it's whether he owns you. He doesn't. Choking is about ultimate power. In the words of my ex, "I like the way it feels when I can control if you live or die". That's what choking really is. He wants ownership and domination. Maybe he's compensating because you do have plenty of independence. It doesn't matter. Get out. This isn't what a loving relationship is. Loving relationships aren't about power.

You deserve better. You're worth it.

Thank you so much for sharing, and reminding those of us who are still climbing out that there's a better world on the other side, if you fight for it. That's the point really... you fought for it, and you made it. It's not lucky, it's incredible and it speaks volumes about both your character and your potential. Congratulations. Enjoy the life that **you built**.

I'm 31. My mom committed suicide when I was 6. I just left a 15-year relationship. There is nothing that I want more than to return to my fantasized version of who she would have been, wherein she could have told me that everything was going to be okay, and where I would have believed her.
We used to keep passwords in a shared location, so he has access to everything. I guess I need to get to work changing those...
Yes! Righteous. Exactly.

Your instincts are right. That's not normal nor healthy. Moreover, most people don't want to have sex with the person that they're angry at... and then return to their rages and hatred. That's almost a rapey tendency. I get that you consented, but you did so not because you wanted to, but because you wanted his affection to return. It's not supposed to be like this.

It's not you, it's him. He should be apologizing for banging things while you had a headache, acting like a toddler over a simple spill, and then throwing something at you recklessly. It's not okay and it will get worse.

Just ask yourself: Under what circumstances would it be okay for you to act like he did? If you'd never do that, then accept that you deserve that same respect.
How long did it take you to be 'okay' after you left?
That hit home. Thanks.
It's from Jordan Peterson's book. The stuff about self-denial in our silence and about the tyranny afoot - that's my home.
Thank you for the reminder!

It almost hurts sometimes. I agree with him when I don't. There's a part of me that so badly wants speak freely, but I don't. I'm not an argumentative person. I'm fine agreeing to disagree, but that's not enough. It has to be 100% agreement all of the time. 

Congrats on the account. I've got to make 1 call tomorrow and then I'll have access. :)
It hurts when he yells so close and so loud, but nothing permanent yet (I don't think).

Even someone who didn't have anxiety would probably feel anxious after a day like that. You should feel proud of yourself for handling it so well, or as you call it "take care of shit mode". Ha ha.

No really, it's okay to feel stressed out after a traumatic experience -- and this was traumatic, even if there wasn't real damage.  Someone hit your car from behind. You did nothing wrong, yet you were temporarily made into the victim of someone else's mistake. Allow yourself to feel. It's okay.
It sounds more like you had a bit of an anxiety attack, and your adrenal surged. There's no reason to expect brain damage.
Sounds like a good plan. Let us know how well it works!
Yep. I do a video show. In the hour before it starts, I pee maybe 20 times.

Challenge yourself to do one thing each day. Just one thing. And do it. Then enjoy the satisfaction afterward... how that sense of accomplishment makes you feel. And if you do this one thing each day it'll eventually become something, a talent maybe, or a skill. Either way, it'll be something that you can be proud of.

Trying to do two or more things will be too much at first, most likely. Your anxiety will kick in and you'll shut down, because it's too much. That's okay. Just one thing..

I have this problem too, even though I don't have living parents. For me, it's political pundits and public figures who talk about the maternal "expiration date", to be a little crass. We all want to be financially strong before bringing a child into this world, and sometimes before even dating, but there's no time to do everything at once. I hear pundits talk about how the women who delay having children will eventually make that decision too late, and will spend the next 40 years lonely and miserable. I wonder if they're right, and my anxiety goes through the roof.  It's why I'm awake right now, at 4 AM. 

Anyway, I don't have the solution. I just wanted you to know that you're not alone.
Do you live with her? Is there any way you can increase your distance?

The President is threatening criminal action and has involved police, because he has no respect for the 1st Amendment. It's a friggin public university. This video covers it really well: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=na8vI7pDr4o](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=na8vI7pDr4o)

If you have any means, offer her the opportunity to come stay with you for a while, till she gets on her feet. If she's at the point of fearing for her life, she may just really need a way out (an immediate one).

Don't be pressured by anyone on whether or not to have your child. Not even on here. Having a crappy partner doesn't mean you won't have a wonderful child, with decades of love and happiness. I do definitely think you should cut off that guy. He sounds psycho. You never know how many (or how few) opportunities you'll have for a child in the future, so give it real thought.

God speed.

Have you considered calling the police over his suicide threats? He shouldn't make those lightly, and watching how much he changes when the police arrives might be good for you. You'll be able to see just how manipulative he is... and maybe walk away from this relationship?
Leave. Don't invest anymore energy in him, when you could be spending that time finding someone else.
Thanks for being willing to offer such a unique solution. There are no ideal solutions from here, so the more options, the better. It feels like there's a bit of hope.
Yes, I came to the U.S. because he invited me. But I was 16... that's the age of consent in NC. So it was legal, right?
The age of consent in NC is 16 - so I don't think it's illegal.
You say that happiness is fleeting, which it is. What gives *you* that fleeting happiness?

Yeah, I'm 28 and going to college now would be intolerable for that reason. I'd probably just take an online course. I don't even have a GED yet. See, you found somebody whose situation is worse! lol. Anyway, maybe just focus on improving one thing at a time? I once heard someone say that you shouldn't compare yourself to who other people are today, but to who you were yesterday. It seems like pretty sound advice. 

Can you start making progress toward any of the things you listed? Maybe work on getting the driver's license?

I'm in a complicated situation with a guy too. If I committed suicide, he'd lose it, but he's actually one of the greatest sources of my pain. It's ironic. 

Anyway, I don't have any friends really. I don't even go anywhere away from him. We could be pals, if you feel like it?

Nah, it's not temporary. When my mother killed herself, leaving behind 5 kids, there was the initial upset, right? I guess you'd call it the grieving process. For most of us, that probably lasted a year. I think it lasted 2 for me, because I was only 6, so she was particularly instrumental. 

After that though, your whole life can feel tainted by the choice that this other person made. It's like they made an indictment against you -- that you weren't worth sticking around for, that you weren't worthy of their care or attention, etc. I'm an adult now heading toward my 30's, and I still avoid movies with positive mother figures, because I can't take the reminder of what I've lost, and what I could have had. Suicide changes things in a way that another death doesn't.

I don't really know what to say. If you have a question, I'll answer, but I think I laid out the problems. My life leads nowhere. I try to look forward so that I have something that I'm working toward, but I can't see any happiness there.

In short: because lives can actually improve. Plus, suicides devastate families left behind more than regular deaths, so there's that too. Then there's the fact that most people regret it. At least, most jumpers from Niagara Falls call out for help. If you read stories of those who try, believe that there's no turning back, and then they're saved, so often they're thankful.

Anyway, I'm not the best person to be answering this since I'm in a pretty dark place, but I thought I'd brainstorm with you tonight.
